sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你既能聆听迷人的故事、了解世界上稀奇古怪的事物，又能同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today is the start of another three-part mini-series, which I am giving the name of Putin and Poison.
sentences.zh: 我是阿拉斯泰尔·巴奇（Alastair Budge），今天是另一场三集迷你系列的开篇，我将其命名为《普京与毒药》（Putin and Poison）。

sentences.en: In part one, this episode, we are going to look at the life of Vladimir Putin, learn about his early life and rise to power, and find out how he went from a small, rat-infested apartment in St Petersburg to the heart of the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分，也就是本期节目中，我们将回顾弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin）的一生，了解他的早年经历与权力崛起之路，并探索他是如何从圣彼得堡一间鼠患横行的简陋公寓，一路走到克里姆林宫核心的。

sentences.en: In part two, we are going to look at a very specific event in the life of Vladimir Putin, the murder by poison of his former colleague and then critic, Alexander Litvinenko.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分中，我们将聚焦普京生平中的一个特定事件——他的前同事、后来的批评者亚历山大·利特维ネン科（Alexander Litvinenko）遭毒杀身亡。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to look at the tragicomic time that two Russian agents travelled to the sleepy town of Salisbury, in England, in a failed attempt to poison a double agent called Sergey Skripal.
sentences.zh: 在第三部分中，我们将讲述一个悲喜交加的故事：两名俄罗斯特工前往英国平静的索尔兹伯里小镇，试图毒害一名名为谢尔盖·斯克里帕尔（Sergey Skripal）的双重间谍，但最终以失败告终。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get started and learn about the life of Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们开始吧，一起来了解弗拉基米尔·普京的人生。

sentences.en: The siege of Leningrad was one of the most brutal events of World War Two.
sentences.zh: 列宁格勒围城战是第二次世界大战中最残酷的事件之一。

sentences.en: From the 8th of September 1941 to the 27th of January 1944, the Russian city now known as St Petersburg was surrounded by German forces, with Finnish troops occupying positions to the north.
sentences.zh: 从1941年9月8日到1944年1月27日，这座如今被称为圣彼得堡的俄罗斯城市被德军重重包围，芬兰军队则占据着北面的阵地。

sentences.en: This siege involved 872 days of non-stop artillery and bombing raids in an attempt to annihilate, to completely destroy, the city and its 3 million residents.
sentences.zh: 这场围城战包含了长达872天不间断的炮击和轰炸，企图彻底消灭、彻底摧毁这座城市及其300万居民。

sentences.en: Alongside this, the winter of 1941 was brutally cold.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，1941年的冬天异常寒冷。

sentences.en: Temperatures dropped to minus 40 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 气温骤降至零下40摄氏度。

sentences.en: Residents were forced to burn books to keep warm.
sentences.zh: 居民们被迫烧书取暖。

sentences.en: Dogs, cats and rats were killed to supplement the miserable 125 grammes of bread a day that each resident was allocated.
sentences.zh: 狗、猫和老鼠都被杀来吃，以勉强维持每人每天仅有125克面包的可怜配给。

sentences.en: An estimated 1.5 million people died, but most not from German bombs or bullets but from starvation.
sentences.zh: 据估计有150万人死亡，但绝大多数死于饥饿，而不是德国的炸弹或子弹。

sentences.en: Early 1942 was particularly brutal, with an estimated 100,000 people dying from starvation every month.
sentences.zh: 1942年初尤其残酷，估计每个月有10万民众死于饥饿。

sentences.en: To put it another way, that’s one person dying from starvation every 25 seconds.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这意味着每25秒就有一个人死于饥饿。

sentences.en: Two people who were lucky enough not to perish were Vladimir Spiridonovich Putin and Maria Ivanovna Putina.
sentences.zh: 有两个人非常幸运，没有死于这场浩劫，他们就是弗拉基米尔·斯皮里多诺维奇·普京（Vladimir Spiridonovich Putin）和玛丽亚·伊万诺夫娜·普京娜（Maria Ivanovna Putina）。

sentences.en: Eight years after the end of the war, in 1952, they had a son.
sentences.zh: 战争结束八年后的1952年，他们迎来了一个儿子。

sentences.en: It was somewhat unexpected. Maria was 41, as was Vladimir, and they had already had two sons, both of whom had died: the first as an infant and the second in the siege of Leningrad.
sentences.zh: 这多少有些出人意料。当时玛丽亚和弗拉基米尔都41岁了，他们之前已经有过两个儿子，但不幸都夭折了：大儿子在婴儿时期夭折，二儿子则死于列宁格勒围城战。

sentences.en: This son’s name, the boy born on October 7th, 1952, was, of course, Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 这个在1952年10月7日出生的男孩的名字，自然就是弗拉基米尔·普京。

sentences.en: There are very few records of the early life of Vladimir Putin, few pictures or official documents, and what we know comes mainly from the man himself.
sentences.zh: 关于弗拉基米尔·普京的早年生活记录极少，照片和官方文件也很匮乏，我们所知道的情况主要来自于他本人的一面之词。

sentences.en: This has led to some conspiracies, including that he was actually born in the Ural Mountains to a different mother, but these don’t have enough evidence for us to warrant giving them any more time than this.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一些阴谋论的产生，比如传说他其实出生在乌拉尔山脉、生母另有其人，但这些说法缺乏足够的证据，不值得我们花更多时间去关注。

sentences.en: Putin grew up in what we would now describe as extreme poverty: living in a communal apartment without heating or its own toilet.
sentences.zh: 普京在如今会被形容为极度贫困的环境中长大：住在没有暖气、也没有独立厕所的合住公寓里。

sentences.en: By his own admission, he was a street kid, living on the streets, learning how to fight and stand up for himself.
sentences.zh: 据他自己承认，他是个街头混混，混迹街头，学会了如何打架和保护自己。

sentences.en: Indeed, one of his favourite anecdotes from this time is a story about chasing the rats that infested his apartment building.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最喜欢讲的关于这段时期的轶事之一，就是关于追赶他所住公寓楼里横行的老鼠的故事。

sentences.en: To quote Putin directly, 'There, on that stair landing, I got a quick and lasting lesson in the meaning of the word "cornered".
sentences.zh: 用普京的原话来说：“在那里的楼梯平台上，我上了一堂生动而持久的课，明白了‘走投无路’这个词的真正含义。”

sentences.en: There were hordes of rats in the front entryway.
sentences.zh: 前厅里有成群结队的老鼠。

sentences.en: My friends and I used to chase them around with sticks.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们经常拿着棍子追打它们。

sentences.en: Once I spotted a huge rat and pursued it down the hall until I drove it into a corner.
sentences.zh: 有一次我发现了一只巨大的老鼠，顺着过道追它，最后把它逼到了一个角落里。

sentences.en: It had nowhere to run. Suddenly it lashed out and threw itself at me.
sentences.zh: 它无路可逃了。突然，它发起狠来，朝我扑了过来。

sentences.en: I was surprised and frightened. Now the rat was chasing me.
sentences.zh: 我又惊又怕。这下变成老鼠在追我了。

sentences.en: It jumped across the landing and down the stairs.
sentences.zh: 它跳过平台，顺着楼梯跑了下去。

sentences.en: Luckily, I was a little faster and I managed to slam the door on its nose.'
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我动作快了一点，总算在它鼻子前把门重重地关上了。”

sentences.en: He tells this story a lot, so he obviously likes it.
sentences.zh: 这个故事他讲了很多次，显然他很喜欢。

sentences.en: Firstly, it reminds the listener of his upbringing as a regular, working-class Russian.
sentences.zh: 首先，这让听众想起了他作为普通工人阶级俄罗斯人的成长背景。

sentences.en: He is like you, he understands the plight of the average Russian because he is one, or perhaps more accurately, he was one.
sentences.zh: 他和你一样，他理解普通俄罗斯人的困境，因为他就是其中之一，或者更准确地说，他曾经是其中之一。

sentences.en: Secondly, it brings to mind the idea of him being a lifelong rat-crusher.
sentences.zh: 其次，这也让人联想到他那“终生捕鼠者”的硬汉形象。

sentences.en: He might have started chasing rats in a squalid Leningrad apartment block, but the “rats” have just changed into his political opponents.
sentences.zh: 他可能是在列宁格勒一处肮脏的公寓楼里开始追捕老鼠的，但那些“老鼠”现在已经变成了他的政敌。

sentences.en: And finally, to his opponents, foreign and domestic, it warns them not to back him into a corner.
sentences.zh: 最后，对于国内外的对手，这警告他们不要把他逼入绝境。

sentences.en: Like the rat, if he has no option to escape, he will attack.
sentences.zh: 就像老鼠一样，如果他没有逃跑的选择，他就会发起攻击。

sentences.en: Or at least, according to many Western commentators, that’s what he wants them to think.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，根据许多西方评论员的看法，这就是他希望别人认为的。

sentences.en: He was, according to his official Kremlin biography, a troublemaker, uninterested in his studies and more interested in fighting and judo than homework.
sentences.zh: 根据克里姆林宫的官方传记，他曾经是个麻烦制造者，对学业不感兴趣，相比家庭作业，他更热衷于打架和柔道。

sentences.en: What he was interested in was the KGB, the Russian secret service.
sentences.zh: 他真正感兴趣的是KGB，也就是俄罗斯的情报机构。

sentences.en: While he was still at high school he knocked on the door of the KGB offices and enquired about how to join, and was basically told to go away and come back once he had graduated from university.
sentences.zh: 当他还在读高中时，他就敲响了KGB办公室的大门，打听如何才能加入，基本上被告知先回去，大学毕业后再来。

sentences.en: He studied law, which he was told gave him the best chance of being accepted to the KGB, and sure enough, after his graduation in 1975, he joined the KGB.
sentences.zh: 他学的是法律，因为有人告诉他，这能给他提供被KGB录取的最大机会，果不其然，在1975年毕业后，他加入了KGB。

sentences.en: Now, the nature of his work at the KGB is a closely guarded secret, but most biographies of Putin suggest that it was a lot less exciting than it might sound.
sentences.zh: 现在，他在KGB的工作性质是一个严守的秘密，但Putin的大多数传记都表明，这项工作远没有听上去那么令人兴奋。

sentences.en: He was based in Russia for the first 10 years and then was in Dresden, in then East Germany, from 1985 to 1990.
sentences.zh: 他在俄罗斯工作了前10年，然后从1985年到1990年在当时的东德德累斯顿工作。

sentences.en: And he wasn’t operating in the shadows, hiding in ditches or secretly breaking into apartments to gain intelligence.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不是在阴影中行动，躲在壕沟里或秘密潜入公寓去获取情报。

sentences.en: According to a 2012 biography by the Russian-American journalist Masha Gessen, and I’m quoting directly, 'Putin and his colleagues were reduced mainly to collecting press clippings, thus contributing to the mountains of useless information produced by the KGB.'
sentences.zh: 根据俄罗斯裔美国记者Masha Gessen在2012年撰写的一本传记，我直接引用：“Putin和他的同事们主要沦为收集剪报，从而为KGB制造的浩瀚无用的信息堆添砖加瓦。”

sentences.en: In other words, he was pushing paper around.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他就是在做一些文书工作。

sentences.en: It was a rather meaningless office job, but the mystique around it later allowed Putin to let people imagine that it might have been something much more important.
sentences.zh: 这是一份毫无意义的办公室工作，但它周围的神秘感后来让Putin得以让人们想象这可能是某种更重要的事情。

sentences.en: Soon after the fall of the Berlin Wall, in 1989, he returned to Russia, before resigning from the KGB in 1991 and finding work in the St Petersburg local government.
sentences.zh: 在1989年柏林墙倒塌后不久，他回到了俄罗斯，随后在1991年辞去了KGB的工作，并在圣彼得堡地方政府找到了工作。

sentences.en: His first significant political role was as an aide to a charismatic man called Anatoly Sobchak, the mayor of St.
sentences.zh: 他的第一个重要政治角色是一位名叫Anatoly Sobchak富有魅力的人的助手，Sobchak是圣彼得堡市长，也是前法学教授。

sentences.en: Petersburg and a former law professor. Putin worked as Sobchak’s right-hand man, officially in charge of foreign relations.
sentences.zh: Putin担任Sobchak的得力助手，官方职务是负责对外关系。

sentences.en: This job involved attracting international business to the city, something that was desperately needed as Russia transitioned from communism to a capitalist economy.
sentences.zh: 这项工作涉及为这座城市吸引国际商业，在俄罗斯从共产主义向资本主义经济转型之际，这正是急需的。

sentences.en: He got a name for himself as being an effective bag-carrier; someone who was reliable, would always do the work, was a safe, unthreatening pair of hands.
sentences.zh: 他为自己赢得了一个精明能干的“提包客”的名声；一个可靠、总能完成工作、让人放心且人畜无害的人。

sentences.en: But in reality, this job gave Putin access to two things that would become central to his later career: connections and control.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这份工作让Putin接触到了对他后来职业生涯至关重要的两样东西：人脉和控制力。

sentences.en: Connections with powerful businesspeople, government officials, and, some would argue, criminal organisations.
sentences.zh: 与有权有势的商人、政府官员以及一些人所说的犯罪组织的人脉。

sentences.en: And control over who got what and under what terms.
sentences.zh: 以及对谁能得到什么、在什么条款下得到的控制权。

sentences.en: It was also during this time that allegations of corruption began to follow him.
sentences.zh: 也正是在这段时间里，有关腐败的指控开始缠上他。

sentences.en: A 1992 investigation accused Putin of allowing raw materials—like metals—to be sold abroad in exchange for food imports that never arrived.
sentences.zh: 1992年的一项调查指控Putin允许将金属等原材料出售到国外，以换取永远没有送到的食品进口。

sentences.en: The amount of money involved was significant, and it painted an early picture of a man willing to bend the rules for those in his circle.
sentences.zh: 涉及的金额巨大，这勾勒出了一个愿意为了自己圈子里的人打破规则的人的早期形象。

sentences.en: However, none of this damaged his career.
sentences.zh: 然而，这一切都没有损害他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Sobchak was loyal to Putin, and in Russian politics, like in many countries, unfortunately, loyalty is often more important than integrity.
sentences.zh: Sobchak对Putin忠心耿耿，而在俄罗斯政坛，和许多国家一样，不幸的是，忠诚往往比清廉更重要。

sentences.en: This loyalty went both ways. When Sobchak lost his position as mayor in 1996, Putin stuck with him.
sentences.zh: 这种忠诚是相互的。当Sobchak在1996年失去市长职位时，Putin一直追随他。

sentences.en: He even helped him flee to Paris when Sobchak faced corruption charges.
sentences.zh: 当Sobchak面临腐败指控时，他甚至帮他逃往巴黎。

sentences.en: Putin, it seemed, was a man who understood the importance of doing favours—and collecting them when the time was right.
sentences.zh: 看起来，Putin是一个深谙投桃报李之道——并在时机成熟时收获回报的人。

sentences.en: In 1996, Vladimir Putin moved to Moscow, leaving behind his relatively modest role in St.
sentences.zh: 1996年，Vladimir Putin搬到了莫斯科，告别了他在圣彼得堡相对低调的角色。

sentences.en: Petersburg. And once in the capital, his career took off at lightning speed.
sentences.zh: 一旦来到首都，他的职业生涯便以闪电般的速度腾飞。

sentences.en: He quickly gained a reputation for being loyal, reliable, and—importantly— unambitious in the eyes of those in power.
sentences.zh: 在当权者眼中，他迅速树立了忠诚、可靠且——重要的是——没有野心的声誉。

sentences.en: This made him the perfect candidate for those looking to elevate someone they could control.
sentences.zh: 这使他成为那些希望提升一个可以由自己掌控的人的完美人选。

sentences.en: In 1998, he was appointed head of the Federal Security Service, or FSB, the successor to the KGB.
sentences.zh: 1998年，他被任命为联邦安全局（即FSB，KGB的继承者）局长。

sentences.en: Just a year later, in 1999, Boris Yeltsin, Russia’s first president, made him prime minister.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一年后的1999年，俄罗斯首任总统Boris Yeltsin任命他为总理。

sentences.en: Putin’s appointment came at a chaotic time for Russia.
sentences.zh: Putin的上台正值俄罗斯局势混乱的时期。

sentences.en: The country was struggling economically, politically, and socially after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 在苏联解体后，该国在经济、政治和社会上面临着重重困境。

sentences.en: Boris Yeltsin himself was deeply unpopular, and his government was plagued by corruption scandals.
sentences.zh: Boris Yeltsin本人极不受欢迎，他的政府也饱受腐败丑闻的困扰。

sentences.en: He was also an awful drunk and was seen as a liability.
sentences.zh: 他也是个臭名昭著的酒鬼，被视为一种累赘。

sentences.en: The sober Putin, on the other hand, presented himself as a calm, no-nonsense figure—a man who could bring order to the chaos.
sentences.zh: 与此形成鲜明对比的是，滴酒不沾的普京把自己塑造成了一个冷静、务实的形象——一个能为混乱带来秩序的人。

sentences.en: His first major test came in 1999, during the Second Chechen War.
sentences.zh: 他的第一个重大考验出现在1999年，即第二次车臣战争期间。

sentences.en: A series of apartment bombings in Russia killed over 300 people, and the government blamed Chechen rebels.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯发生了一系列公寓爆炸案，导致300多人丧生，政府将此归咎于车臣叛军。

sentences.en: Putin’s response was swift and brutal. He promised to hunt down the perpetrators, famously declaring, “We will pursue terrorists everywhere.
sentences.zh: 普京的反应迅速而残酷。他承诺将追捕肇事者，并说出了那句名言：“我们将到处追捕恐怖分子。

sentences.en: If we catch them in the toilet, we’ll drown them there.”
sentences.zh: 如果我们把他们在厕所里抓到，我们就会把他们淹死在那里。”

sentences.en: This tough rhetoric and his decisive actions won him widespread support.
sentences.zh: 这种强硬的言论和果断的行动赢得了他广泛的支持。

sentences.en: To many Russians, especially compared to the permanently drunk and unreliable Yeltsin, he seemed like the strong leader the country desperately needed.
sentences.zh: 对于许多俄罗斯人来说，尤其是与那个终日酗酒、靠不住的叶利钦相比，他似乎正是国家急需的强力领袖。

sentences.en: Then, on New Year’s Eve 1999, Boris Yeltsin resigned as president.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1999年的除夕夜，叶利钦辞去了总统职务。

sentences.en: In a surprising and dramatic announcement, in which he talked about the need for Russia to move into the new millennium with new leaders, he handed power to Putin, who became acting president.
sentences.zh: 在一项令人惊讶且戏剧性的声明中，他谈到俄罗斯需要由新一代领导人带领跨入新千年，随后他将权力移交给了普京，普京由此成为代总统。

sentences.en: At that moment, Vladimir Putin, a man who had risen from obscurity, and was partly given positions of power because he was thought not to want it, was now the leader of Russia.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，弗拉基米尔·普京——一个从籍籍无名中崛起、当初部分是因为人们认为他没有对权力的野心才被提拔的人——现在成为了俄罗斯的领导人。

sentences.en: Just a few months later, in March of 2000, and in no small part thanks to his perception as being someone who could effectively deal with Chechnya, he won the Presidential election, becoming the duly elected leader of the country.
sentences.zh: 短短几个月后，即2000年3月，很大程度上由于他被认为能够有效处理车臣问题，他赢得了总统大选，成为国家名正言顺的领导人。

sentences.en: When Putin officially became president in 2000, Russia was in disarray.
sentences.zh: 当普京于2000年正式就任总统时，俄罗斯正处于一片混乱之中。

sentences.en: The economy had collapsed following the financial crisis of 1998, oligarchs were running the country, and there was widespread disillusionment with the government.
sentences.zh: 在1998年的金融危机之后，经济已经崩溃，寡头们把持着国家，民众对政府普遍感到失望。

sentences.en: Putin quickly moved to restore order. One of his first targets was the oligarchs —Russia’s super-rich businesspeople who had amassed enormous wealth during the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 普京迅速采取行动恢复秩序。他的首要目标之一就是寡头——那些在20世纪90年代积累了巨额财富的俄罗斯超级富豪。

sentences.en: Some oligarchs, like Roman Abramovich, struck deals with Putin, pledging their loyalty in exchange for keeping their fortunes.
sentences.zh: 一些寡头，比如罗曼·阿布拉莫维奇，与普京达成了协议，宣誓效忠以换取保留他们的财富。

sentences.en: Others, like Mikhail Khodorkovsky, were less fortunate.
sentences.zh: 另一些人，比如米哈伊尔·霍多尔夫斯基，则没有那么幸运。

sentences.en: Khodorkovsky, once the richest man in Russia, was arrested and subjected to a show trial, where this billionaire was placed in a cage in court.
sentences.zh: 霍多尔夫斯基曾是俄罗斯首富，他被捕并经历了一场表演式审判，这位亿万富翁被关在法庭的铁笼里。

sentences.en: Unsurprisingly, he was found guilty, imprisoned, and his company taken over by the state.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外地，他被判有罪并入狱，他的公司也被国家接管。

sentences.en: This sent a clear message: in Putin’s Russia, no one was above the law—unless, of course, you were loyal to Putin.
sentences.zh: 这传递出一个明确的信号：在普京的俄罗斯，没有人能凌驾于法律之上——当然，除非你效忠于普京。

sentences.en: At the same time, Putin worked to consolidate political power.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，普京致力于巩固政治权力。

sentences.en: Independent media outlets were shut down or taken over by state-run companies, political opponents were sidelined or had unfortunate tumbles out of fourth-floor windows, and protests were suppressed.
sentences.zh: 独立的媒体被关闭或由国企接管，政治对手被边缘化，或者“不幸地”从四楼窗户跌落，抗议活动遭到镇压。

sentences.en: But while critics both at home and abroad accused him of authoritarianism, many Russians supported him.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管国内外的批评者谴责他是独裁者，许多俄罗斯人却支持他。

sentences.en: Putin’s first term as President coincided with a boom in oil prices, which was very good news for a country where oil and gas make up a fifth of the economy.
sentences.zh: 普京的第一任总统刚好赶上了油价暴涨，对于一个石油和天然气占经济五分之一的国家来说，这无疑是个好消息。

sentences.en: Under Putin, the economy stabilised, and living standards improved, at least in the early years.
sentences.zh: 在普京的领导下，经济趋于稳定，生活水平有所提高，至少在早期是这样的。

sentences.en: He positioned himself as the man who had restored Russia’s pride and power.
sentences.zh: 把自己定位为恢复俄罗斯尊严和力量的人。

sentences.en: He also cultivated a very specific image of himself: the fearless leader.
sentences.zh: 他还精心打造了一个非常独特的个人形象：无所畏惧的领袖。

sentences.en: He was photographed riding horses shirtless, diving into icy waters, and piloting fighter jets.
sentences.zh: 镜头记录下他赤膊骑马、冬泳以及驾驶战斗机的画面。

sentences.en: This was especially the case during his brief hiatus from the Presidency, when after serving for two terms, he stepped down as President, as required by the Russian constitution, and his ally, Dmitry Medvedev, became President.
sentences.zh: 在他短暂离开总统宝座期间尤其如此：根据俄罗斯宪法规定，在连任两届后他卸任总统，他的盟友德米特里·梅德韦杰夫成为了总统。

sentences.en: As you may remember, this was in 2008, and at the time, there was reportedly a popular joke being told by Russians that gives you some indication of who people thought was really in charge.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，那是2008年，当时据报道俄罗斯流传着一个笑话，能让你大致看出人们认为究竟是谁在掌权。

sentences.en: And the joke goes something like this: Prime Minister Vladimir Putin gave Medvedev a car without a steering wheel.
sentences.zh: 这个笑话大致是这样的：时任总理弗拉基米尔·普京给梅德韦杰夫车里配了一个没有方向盘的汽车。

sentences.en: Medvedev gets into the car, then says “But where is the steering wheel?”
sentences.zh: 梅德韦杰夫上车后说：“但是方向盘在哪里呢？”

sentences.en: “Don’t worry,” answers Putin. “I’ll be doing the driving.”
sentences.zh: 普京回答说：“别担心，我来开车。”

sentences.en: After this brief 4-year period ostensibly not running the country, Putin was re-elected as President in 2012, and he has been running the country ever since.
sentences.zh: 在经历了这表面上4年不直接掌管国家的短暂时期后，普京在2012年重新当选总统，并从那时起一直掌管着这个国家。

sentences.en: In 2020, he even pushed through a constitutional amendment meaning that, theoretically, at least, he could remain President until the year 2036.
sentences.zh: 在2020年，他甚至强行推动了一项宪法修正案，理论上讲，他至少可以一直担任总统到2036年。

sentences.en: Now, in the incredibly unlikely case that you'd never heard of Vladimir Putin before this, you might have thought that he sounds like an effective, strong leader, and there’s not much more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 现在，在极不可能的情况下，如果你在此之前从未听说过弗拉基米尔·普京，你可能会觉得他听起来像一个高效、强势的领导人，事情仅此而已。

sentences.en: But, of course, the path to get here, and what he has done to maintain his power, has come at a brutal cost.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，走到这一步的道路，以及他为了维持权力所做的事情，付出了残酷的代价。

sentences.en: One of the most controversial moments early in his rise to power came in 1999, during the wave of apartment bombings that killed over 300 people in cities across Russia.
sentences.zh: 在他崛起之初最具争议的时刻之一发生在1999年，当时俄罗斯各大城市发生了导致300多人丧生的连环公寓爆炸案。

sentences.en: These bombings, which the government blamed on Chechen rebels, provided the justification for Putin’s launch of the Second Chechen War, a brutal military campaign to bring the region back under Russian control.
sentences.zh: 政府将这些爆炸案归咎于车臣叛军，这为普京发动第二次车臣战争提供了借口，这是一场旨在将该地区重新置于俄罗斯控制之下的残酷军事行动。

sentences.en: But suspicions have lingered that the bombings were not the work of Chechen terrorists but a false flag operation orchestrated by Russia’s own security services to justify the war and bolster Putin’s image as a strong leader.
sentences.zh: 然而，外界一直怀疑这些爆炸案并非车臣恐怖分子所为，而是由俄罗斯自身安全部门精心策划的“假旗行动”，旨在为战争制造借口并树立普京作为强力领袖的形象。

sentences.en: In other words, these bombings were not the work of Chechen terrorists but of the FSB, on Putin’s orders, and hundreds of innocent Russian citizens were murdered to provide justification for a war in Chechnya.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些爆炸案不是车臣恐怖分子干的，而是FSB在普京的命令下实施的，数百名无辜的俄罗斯平民被谋杀，仅仅是为了给发动车臣战争提供借口。

sentences.en: On one occasion, for example, bombs were found under an apartment block, and FSB agents were seen placing them, but when pressed, the government said that it was simply a training exercise.
sentences.zh: 例如，曾有一次，人们在一栋公寓楼下发现了炸弹，并看到FSB特工在安放炸弹，但当受到追问时，政府却声称这只是一次军事演习。

sentences.en: Not everyone is convinced, and the Kremlin denies it vehemently, but the bombings remain a dark shadow over Putin’s rise to power, and the truth remains a subject of debate.
sentences.zh: 并非所有人都买账，克里姆林宫也对此进行了坚决否认，但爆炸案依然是普京崛起之路上的一道阴影，真相至今仍是争论的话题。

sentences.en: The Second Chechen War that followed was marked by extreme brutality.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的第二次车臣战争以极其残暴著称。

sentences.en: The Russian military indiscriminately bombed Chechen cities, including Grozny, the capital, which was described by the United Nations as the most destroyed city on Earth at the time.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯军队无差别地轰炸车臣城市，包括首都格罗兹尼，被联合国形容为当时地球上被毁得最严重的城市。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of civilians were killed, and reports of war crimes, including torture and summary executions, were widespread.
sentences.zh: 数万名平民丧生，有关酷刑和即决处决等战争罪行的报道比比皆是。

sentences.en: This approach sent a clear message: dissent would not be tolerated, and no price was too high to maintain Russia’s territorial integrity and Putin’s grip on power.
sentences.zh: 这种做法传递出一个明确的信号：异见绝不被容忍，为了维持俄罗斯的领土完整和普京对权力的掌控，付出任何代价都在所不惜。

sentences.en: And for anybody who did violate this message, anyone who stood against him, there were no lengths that Putin was not willing to go to to silence them.
sentences.zh: 而对于任何敢于违背这一信号、任何敢于与他作对的人，普京为了让他们闭嘴，会不择一切手段。

sentences.en: You could run, you could hide, but eventually, Putin would get you.
sentences.zh: 你可以跑，你可以躲，但最终，普京还是会找到你。

sentences.en: One of his weapons of choice, at least to knock off individuals, is the theme of the next two episodes: poison.
sentences.zh: 他用来消灭异己的首选武器之一，也是接下来两集的主题：毒药。

sentences.en: In 2006, a former FSB agent turned critic called Alexander Litvinenko made the mistake of going for tea with a couple of Russian agents in a five star hotel in Mayfair, in London.
sentences.zh: 2006年，一个倒戈的FSB前特工亚历山大·利特维年科犯了一个错误，他在伦敦梅菲尔区的一家五星级酒店里和几个俄罗斯特工一起喝了茶。

sentences.en: The green tea contained polonium-210, a radioactive element, and three weeks later, after a drawn out and very public decline, he died.
sentences.zh: 这杯绿茶里含有钋-210，这是一种放射性元素，三周后，在经历了一场漫长而广为人知的健康恶化后，他死了。

sentences.en: Twelve years later, in 2018, Russian agents travelled to the UK again in an attempt to poison another former Russian agent, Sergey Skripal, but they failed in their attempt.
sentences.zh: 十二年后的2018年，俄罗斯特工再次前往英国，试图毒害另一名俄罗斯前特工谢尔盖·斯克里帕尔，但他们的企图失败了。

sentences.en: We’ll cover these incidents in much greater detail in parts two and three of this mini-series, and they are only a couple in a long list of the use of poison under Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本迷你系列的第二部分和第三部分中更详细地探讨这些事件，而在弗拉基米尔·普京统治下使用毒药的长长名单中，这只是其中冰山一角。

sentences.en: These incidents not only silence critics but also serve as a warning to others: defy the Kremlin at your own risk.
sentences.zh: 这些事件不仅让批评者闭嘴，也对其他人起到了警示作用：挑战克里姆林宫，后果自负。

sentences.en: But perhaps the most chilling example of Putin’s ruthlessness has been his invasion of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 但普京冷酷无情最令人毛骨悚然的例子，或许莫过于他对乌克兰的入侵。

sentences.en: In 2014, Russia annexed Crimea, a move that shocked the world and drew condemnation from Western nations.
sentences.zh: 2014年，俄罗斯吞并了克里米亚，此举震惊了世界，并招致西方国家的谴责。

sentences.en: Then, in February 2022, Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, bizarrely claiming it was to “denazify” the country and protect Russian-speaking populations.
sentences.zh: 然后，在2022年2月，普京对乌克兰发起了全面入侵，荒谬地声称这是为了“去纳粹化”该国并保护俄语人口。

sentences.en: What followed, as you will know, was a brutal war that has displaced millions, caused tens of thousands of deaths, and left parts of Ukraine in ruins.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，随之而来的是一场残酷的战争，数百万人流离失所，数万人死亡，乌克兰部分地区沦为废墟。

sentences.en: The invasion, which was widely seen as an attempt to reassert Russia’s influence and challenge NATO’s expansion, has plunged relations between Russia and the West to their lowest point since the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 这场入侵被普遍视为重塑俄罗斯影响力并挑战北约扩张的企图，它将俄乌以及俄罗斯与西方国家的关系降到了冷战以来的最低点。

sentences.en: And it has further isolated Russia economically and politically, raising questions about Putin’s long-term strategy and the future of his regime.
sentences.zh: 这进一步孤立了俄罗斯的经济和政治，引发了人们对普京长期战略及其政权未来的性质疑。

sentences.en: But throughout all of this—wars, poisonings, and repression—Putin has shown an unrelenting commitment to holding onto power.
sentences.zh: 然而，贯穿这一切——战争、投毒和镇压——普京表现出了对权力恋栈不去的坚定决心。

sentences.en: For his supporters, these actions are the price of protecting Russia’s sovereignty and status as a global power.
sentences.zh: 对于他的支持者来说，这些行动是捍卫俄罗斯主权和全球大国地位必须付出的代价。

sentences.en: For his critics, they are the hallmarks of a man willing to destroy anyone or anything that stands in his way.
sentences.zh: 对于他的批评者来说，这是一个愿意摧毁任何阻碍他道路的人或事的独裁者的特征。

sentences.en: As of the start of 2025, Vladimir Putin has been in power for 25 years, longer than many of the tsars who ruled Russia before him.
sentences.zh: 截至2025年初，弗拉基米尔·普京已经执政25年，超过了许多在他之前统治俄罗斯的沙皇。

sentences.en: His life, from the streets of Leningrad to the Kremlin, is a story of ambition, secrecy, and survival at all costs.
sentences.zh: 他的人生，从列宁格勒的街头到克里姆林宫，是一个关于野心、秘密以及不惜一切代价求生存的故事。

sentences.en: But as Russia faces growing challenges at home and abroad, questions are emerging about how long this can continue.
sentences.zh: 但随着俄罗斯面临来自国内外的日益严峻的挑战，人们开始质疑这种状态还能持续多久。

sentences.en: Will Putin’s legacy be that of a man who restored Russia’s pride and power?
sentences.zh: 普京留下的政治遗产，会是一个恢复了俄罗斯尊严和力量的人吗？

sentences.en: Or will he be remembered as the leader who isolated his country and left it in ruins?
sentences.zh: 还是会被铭记为那个孤立国家并将其化为废墟的领导人？

sentences.en: To wrap things up, Vladimir Putin has shaped modern Russia in his image.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，弗拉基米尔·普京按照自己的形象塑造了现代俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He is 72 years old, shows no signs of relinquishing power, and if he rules for another 5 years, he will eclipse Josef Stalin as Russia’s longest-serving leader.
sentences.zh: 他已经72岁了，没有表现出任何放弃权力的迹象，如果他再统治5年，他将超越约瑟夫·斯大林，成为俄罗斯执政时间最长的领导人。

sentences.en: One thing seems clear: for better or for worse, the story of Vladimir Putin is far from over.
sentences.zh: 有一点似乎很清楚：无论好坏，弗拉基米尔·普京的故事远未结束。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于弗拉基米尔·普京的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: To state the obvious, we have only scratched the surface on the life of this man; hundreds of thousands of pages have been written, and I hope you will forgive me for skimming over many important and fascinating elements.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，我们只是触及了这个人一生的冰山一角；相关文字记录多达几十万页，希望大家原谅我略过了许多重要且引人入胜的细节。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this is part one of a three part mini-series on Putin and Poison, and in parts two and three we are going to go a lot deeper into two different but closely related incidents widely believed to be ordered by Vladimir Putin himself: the poisoning of one of his fiercest critics, Alexander Litvinenko, and the failed murder attempt on a former double agent, Sergey Skripal.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于普京与毒药的三集迷你系列的第一部分，在第二部分和第三部分中，我们将更深入地探讨两起不同但密切相关的事件，人们普遍认为这些事件是弗拉基米尔·普京本人下令实施的：毒害他最激烈的批评者之一亚历山大·利特维年科，以及对前双重间谍谢尔盖·斯克里帕尔的未遂谋杀。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 您收听的是由《Leonardo English》制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是阿拉斯泰尔·布迪（Alastair Budge），请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
